Subject: Quick ask: pilot hosting posture for an isolated EHR workload

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

We're lining up a small pilot for our clinical summarization agent and need advice on whether to start on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or go straight to a Private deployment (VPC, customer-controlled) given our compliance constraints. A few quick stats:
- Expected steady-state: ~18 qps (avg inference requests) with 2.7k tokens / request
- Peak concurrency: 55 concurrent sessions during clinic hours
- Models: ensemble with a 13B open model + a lightweight reranker
- Data: PHI, must meet our internal audit and retention controls

Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks; if pilot succeeds we'd scale to production in ~5 months.

Key asks: recommended starting posture (Dedicated vs Private), rough capacity footprint, and lead times. We also want any notes on fallback/escape hatches if we hit load spikes.

Thanks,
Leah
Leah Burns
Director, Clinical Innovation
Accordia Health

Hi Leah — thanks for the details, this is helpful. Short answer: for a 6–8 week pilot we usually recommend starting on Dedicated reserved capacity and reserve the Private option as a post-pilot migration for full production.

Why Dedicated first (high-level):
- Faster lead time (2–3 weeks to provision a committed slice) vs Private which often takes 6–10 weeks for VPC + security onboarding.
- Predictable throughput for pilot benchmarks, easier to instrument cost/latency.
- We can configure strict tenancy boundaries and per-deal KV prefixing to reduce data bleed risk during pilot.

We can put together a quick capacity model and an escape hatch (burst-to-private / fallback to smaller models) plan — attaching a first-pass workbook. Can you confirm average token distribution (50% <1k, 30% 1–3k, 20% >3k) and whether you need SOC 2 evidence packaged with the pilot engagement?

Draft attached: Accordia_MVP_capacity_model.xlsx (first-pass).

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Notes after quick sizing pass (numbers are conservative for pilot burst protection):
- Suggested reserved slate for pilot (3 months): 8 x A10G-equivalent instances (continuous) + 2 x A10G-equivalent burst nodes. This gives headroom for 55 concurrency with ensemble + reranker when we batch efficiently.
- Expected token throughput: ~45M tokens/day given usage profile; estimated pilot monthly compute cost (Reserved + burst + infra) ≈ $26k–$34k depending on batching/quantization choices.
- Lead time: reserved capacity slice = 10 business days to lock & provision; enabling burst/escape capacity typically 3–5 business days after slice provision.

Compliance/ops: attached SOC2 evidence summary and a one-page Dedicated-runbook template for audit purposes. For pilot-level PHI handling we recommend:
- Enable per-deal KV prefixes + enforced TTLs
- Audit log forwarding to Accordia syslog endpoint (or S3 with HSM keys)
- Minimum retention policy 90 days for token logs unless otherwise requested

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf; I've also added a simplified cost tab in the workbook.

—Marissa

Subject: Recommendation: Dedicated pilot with Private migration path — Accordia Health (ACC-9831)

Hi Leah — following up with a recommended path and the operational tradeoffs so you can take this to your procurement and security teams. TL;DR: start the pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity, instrument rigorously, and plan a staged migration to Private for full production if you require customer-managed networking or additional isolation controls.

Recommendation summary:
- Pilot posture: Redwood Dedicated (3-month reserved slice)
- Proposed slate: 8 reserved A10G-equivalent nodes + 2 burst nodes (handles 55 concurrency and 13B ensemble with batching)
- Estimated monthly pilot cost: $26k–$34k (includes datastore, logs export, and basic monitoring)
- Lead times: reserve lock and provisioning ~10 business days once PO in; security onboarding for Private later adds ~4–8 additional weeks.

Why this path works:
1) Speed: Dedicated gets you measurable SLA and throughput quickly so the clinical teams can evaluate model quality under realistic load.
2) Observability: we can enable token-level cost/latency dashboards and run the same eval harness across Dedicated and Private to avoid regressions.
3) Migration: when you're ready for production we execute a migration plan that preserves model versions and routing policies — the primary lift is network & key management.

Escape hatch (if you hit unexpected spikes):
- Auto-burst to pre-approved on-demand nodes (capacity & credit guardrails)
- Fallback model bundle with cheaper quantized variant for non-critical paths

Next steps / ask list:
1) Confirm token distribution breakouts (50% low / 30% mid / 20% high) or send real trace.
2) Confirm procurement PO window and preferred billing cadence.
3) If you want Private in parallel, we can start the security questionnaire now to compress later lead time.

I've attached the updated workbook and the SOC2 summary. Also linking the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACC-9831.

If this looks good I can spin up a formal SOW and an RFC for the Dedicated slice.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
